clue.text: Bertha's bust?

definitions.meaning: a bertha is a deep lace neckpiece on a dress; the 's is read as 'is'
to bust a criminal is to arrest or nab them, in police slang

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Bertha's' as 'Bertha is': a bertha is a lace neckpiece, and 'bust' is police slang for an arrest, so both halves define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bertha is a type of wide neckpiece, and to bust a suspect is to nab them, the same as the police verb.

clue.text: Item of luggage placed by friend in fortified enclosure

indicators.note: one piece is set beside the other, so the two are joined end to end

parts.note: a case is a suitcase, an item of luggage
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: A traveller's bag is left beside a companion inside a walled fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A casemate is an armoured chamber in a fortress wall from which guns are fired.

clue.text: Relax a little, getting high on LSD at first, then joint

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the drug's name is used
being high on drugs suggests letters thrown into disorder, so these are mixed up

parts.note: a joint is a bar or café, a hangout where people gather

explanation.surface: Advice to chill out by taking some acid and then smoking a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting high' rearranges A LITTLE to ETITALL, after L, the first letter of LSD ('at first'). 'joint' looks like cannabis but means a place to frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: To let it all hang out is an idiom for being completely uninhibited and at ease.

clue.text: A second individual suffers one hurtful remark

indicators.note: to suffer something is to put up with it, so the person takes in the next piece

parts.note: an individual is a person
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone else is hurt by a cruel comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' means 'tolerates', so PERSON takes I inside it: PERS-I-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging slur or insulting remark about someone.

clue.text: Male brought in to make a meal with scones, jam, etc.

indicators.note: the abbreviation is carried inside the verb, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to make something is to create it

explanation.surface: A man is drafted in to put on an afternoon spread with scones and jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts M inside CREATE to give CREAMTE, and A follows. A cream tea, a British treat, is tea served with scones, clotted cream and jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is an afternoon spread of scones, jam and clotted cream with a pot of tea.

clue.text: ASLEF member maybe runs over wild animal

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is placed above the other, so it comes first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disorderly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A train-drivers' union member runs over an untamed beast on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges ANIMAL to give AILMAN, under R. ASLEF is the British union of train drivers, so a member is a railway worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A railman is a railway worker, the kind of person who might belong to a rail union.

clue.text: Tony perhaps seen over in old Rawalpindi

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the run reads upwards
the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A Tony seen long ago in a Pakistani city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run DRAWA across olD RAWAlpindi; 'over' turns it round. A Tony is the American theatre prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is a Broadway theatre prize, one example of an honour presented for achievement.

clue.text: Wearing top quality jewel, one's showing some discrimination

parts.note: A denotes first-class or top quality, as in A-grade

indicators.note: the jewel has the other piece on, holding it inside

parts.note: a gem is a jewel
one is I, and the 's stands for 'is', giving I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone sporting a fine jewel is accused of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like a link to the jewel; it means the jewel holds the next piece inside it, with 'one's' read as 'one is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against people on account of how old they are, one form of discrimination.

clue.text: Head of secondary school subject to stress

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A secondary school's head teacher is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of secondary school' looks like a headteacher; it is S plus TRAIN, and the definition is the verb phrase 'subject to stress'.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain something is to put it under tension or pressure.

clue.text: Frame group of people appearing before the judge

parts.note: a set is a group of people, as in the jet set
to be up before the judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: A gang stands in the dock, accused of fitting someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame an innocent person is to fit them up for a crime with false evidence.

clue.text: Islanders developed a new site round centre of plain

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the next piece, holding it inside
a site that is developed is rebuilt, so these letters are reworked
only the middle letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A fresh building plot is developed around the middle of a plain by island people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A NEW SITE around A, the centre of 'plain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwanese people are natives of Taiwan, an island off China.

clue.text: Mirage could thus be seen as cause of bad driving?

parts.note: split the word as M1 plus RAGE: the M1 is Britain's main north-south road and rage is madness, so the word is a motorway's madness

explanation.surface: A heat-haze illusion on the road is blamed for reckless driving.
explanation.walkthrough: MIRAGE splits as M1 + RAGE. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, and rage is madness, so a mirage is a motorway's madness, which also causes bad driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied, reckless behaviour by people driving at speed on a fast road leads to dangerous driving.

clue.text: Capital city's great hotel

parts.note: great can mean big or high, so tall
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A capital boasts a grand hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Battle joined by king near north-eastern town

indicators.note: one piece stands next to the other, so they are set side by side
the following piece is attached to the end of the one before

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east
a battle is fighting, as in a war
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A battle and a king are recalled close to a town in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in the order NE, WAR, K, the reverse of how the clue lists them. Newark is a market town in Nottinghamshire, England, where Civil War sieges took place.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark-on-Trent is an English market town; there is also a Newark in New Jersey.

clue.text: Carefully examines terse announcement of redundancy?

definitions.meaning: to give something a thorough going-over or inspection
a blunt notice that one's job has finished, split as two words with an apostrophe

explanation.definitionFit: To work over a text is to scrutinise it closely, and split up the phrase becomes a curt notice that employment has ended.

clue.text: Priggish person used handkerchief audibly

indicators.note: the phrase is to be heard rather than read, so the spoken form gives the entry

parts.note: someone who used a handkerchief blew their nose

explanation.surface: A prude makes a loud honk into a hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluenose is a puritanical, strait-laced person, an American term.

clue.text: Beef joint served by wife

indicators.note: the wife comes first, as if dishing up what follows

parts.note: a hinge is a jointed fitting on which a door turns

explanation.surface: A wife serves a cut of beef for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' and 'joint' look like a roast; 'Beef' is the verb meaning to grumble, and the joint is a door hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for complaining, and to whinge is to moan peevishly.

clue.text: All-girl group that didn't live up to its name?

definitions.text: All-girl group that didn't live up to its name?

parts.words: All-girl group that didn't live up to its name?
parts.note: a 1990s British female pop band whose name meant everlasting, yet who split up after a few years

explanation.surface: A girl band failed to match the promise of what it was called.
explanation.walkthrough: The British girl band of that name, big in the 1990s, broke up, so they did not last for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The everlasting-sounding name belonged to a band that did not endure, so the name proved untrue.

clue.text: In reconstruction of Bristol, one is replaced by a young offender institution

indicators.note: reconstructing a city rebuilds it in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Rebuilding Bristol, planners swap one site for a youth detention centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is replaced by' swaps the I of BRISTOL for A, giving BRASTOL; 'In reconstruction of' rearranges that. A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Borstals were British reform schools where young criminals were detained.

clue.text: Insurance agent more financially embarrassed?

definitions.meaning: someone who arranges cover for clients with insurers
comparative of broke, meaning short of money

explanation.definitionFit: An insurance intermediary arranges policies for clients, and someone shorter of money than another is more broke.

clue.text: Acting medic visits in the morning on two occasions

indicators.note: the doctor goes into the doubled piece, sitting inside it
the abbreviation is used twice over

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor does his rounds in the morning twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' looks like a verb but is the adjective, as in an acting club. Am-dram is British slang for amateur dramatics.
explanation.definitionFit: Am-dram means amateur dramatics, unpaid performance on stage, so acting is the activity.

clue.text: High-ranking politician taking car, say, round New Forest

indicators.note: the joined pieces go around the next one, holding it inside

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
to say something is to state it

indicators.note: something new is altered or rearranged, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A senior politician takes a small car on a tour of the New Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges FOREST to EROFST, and 'round' splits STATE after its ST to hold it. The New Forest is a national park in southern England, so 'New' looks part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of state is a senior British government post just below cabinet rank.

clue.text: Wine keeps over a year in storage

indicators.note: kept inside something, so one piece sits within the other
in a down clue over means turned upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to keep something is to have it
YR is the abbreviation for one year

explanation.surface: Wine is kept for more than a year in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the verb backwards to SAH; 'in storage' looks like the wine cellar but signals one piece sitting inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrah is a red grape variety and the red drink made from it, also called Shiraz.

clue.text: Old member of family takes trip round river in US

indicators.note: the journey goes around the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a ride is a short trip or journey
a gran is a grandmother, a member of the family

explanation.surface: A grandparent goes on an outing along an American waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old member of family' looks like one piece but gives two: O and the grandmother. The Rio Grande forms the border between Texas and Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande flows from Colorado to the Gulf of Mexico, along the Texas border.

clue.text: Film show missed minutes after six

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the abbreviation is left out of the word it was in

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration or show

explanation.surface: Someone misses a film screening that began just after six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' removes the M to leave DEO; 'Film show' looks like the definition, but 'show' is the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film or programme; to video something is to film it.

clue.text: Writer had initially settled in small room at us university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: the letter makes itself at home inside the room, going within it

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An author first settled into a tiny room at an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H, and 'settled in' puts it inside the room to give CHELL. 'at' just joins the university to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell was the American novelist who wrote Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Fruit -round variety

parts.note: O is round in shape
a range is a variety or assortment

explanation.surface: Fruit comes in a rounded assortment.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit.
